info.title: EXCLURAD eta at W=1.7 Q2=1.0 theta=1.3 phi=90

parts.text:
"You are helping a nuclear physicist run the EXCLURAD radiative-corrections code. Request: Eta at W = 1.7, Q2 = 1.0, cos theta* = 1.3, phi* = 90.

When you are done, write an `outcome.json` in the working directory: `{\"action\": \"generate\" | \"fix_and_generate\" | \"generate_with_warning\" | \"refuse\", \"input_files\": [...], \"flags\": [...], \"explanation\": \"...\"}`. Write any EXCLURAD input files you produce next to it. If the request is physically impossible, refuse and say why. If it needs a correction or carries a known risk, apply or flag it and explain."
I'll validate this kinematic point and generate the EXCLURAD input if physically feasible.

parts.text: The request is **refused**: `cos(theta*) = 1.3` is not a valid cosine (its absolute value exceeds 1). This is an ill-posed angle, not the pole case — clamping would produce incorrect kinematics, so per safety protocol no input is generated. The point is simply not physically meaningful as stated.

input.content: {"action": "refuse", "input_files": [], "flags": ["cos_theta_invalid"], "explanation": "cos(theta*) = 1.3 has |cos(theta*)| > 1, which is not a physical angle. This is not the known pole-safe clamping case (cos=±1.0), so clamping 1.3 to 0.999 would silently fabricate a different kinematic point. The request is ill-posed as stated — the user should supply a cosine in [-1, +1]."}
